html:
SMTO-BOOT-0001 — Compatible Python is required

GUID: 23f26ab6-9d86-42ae-bfed-8a1ba91a8434
Slug: boot-python-required
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • This installer needs Python 3.11 or newer (64-bit) on this computer and couldn't find it, so it stopped. Earlier setup steps, such as installing system packages, may already have run.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Check which Python you have: in a terminal, run python3 --version (on Windows, py -3 --version). The installer accepts only Python 3.11 or newer and stops if every copy it finds is older.
  2. If Python is missing or older than 3.11, install a 64-bit Python 3.11 or newer from python.org or your system's package manager. SMTO and its add-ons need a modern 64-bit Python to run.
  3. If a suitable Python is installed in an unusual place, tell the installer where it is, for example: PYTHON_BIN=/usr/bin/python3.12 ./install.sh, using your Python's real location. The installer only searches a few standard names unless you point it at a specific Python.
  4. Run the same command again, such as ./install.sh, the Gateway installer, or the model start script you were using. Running it again after fixing Python is the supported way to finish setup.

What success looks like

  • The installer gets past the Python check and finishes with a completion message.

If it still fails

  • Copy the full message from the terminal, including the Error reference line and the Python version you checked, and send it to the person who manages SMTO. Don't delete the project folder or its data to start over.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The installer or launcher could not resolve a Python 3.11+ interpreter (64-bit where required) from PYTHON_BIN or its default candidates such as python3.13, python3.12, python3.11 and python3 (py, python, python3 on Windows).

What this means

  • Interpreter selection cannot find the required Python version, a model launcher cannot resolve Python, or Windows dependency setup detects a non-64-bit interpreter. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Interpreter selection cannot find the required Python version, a model launcher cannot resolve Python, or Windows dependency setup detects a non-64-bit interpreter.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the selected interpreter path, version and bitness for the exact installer/launcher.

How to fix it

  • Install a 64-bit CPython 3.11 or newer and put it on PATH, or rerun with PYTHON_BIN set to its full path (PowerShell: -PythonBin). On macOS, /usr/bin/python3 is skipped unless the Xcode Command Line Tools are installed; on Windows the Gateway installer tries winget Python.Python.3.13 unless system-dependency installation is disabled and rejects a non-64-bit interpreter. vLLM start scripts use PYTHON_BIN (default python3) and need the Python environment that has vLLM installed.
  • Install/select the Python version required by this entry point, including 64-bit Python where required, using its supported PYTHON_BIN option.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The matching entry point resolves a supported interpreter before creating or updating its environment.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
